role: authoring guide, published to other teams
how_to_score: This is read by people outside this platform, building against the contract. It cannot be scored from our event log — no block team's authoring session appears there. It is scored against the conformance results and defects of the blocks that were built with it: the guide's job is to prevent the failures we keep finding.

dimensions.name: Prevents the failures we actually see
dimensions.evidence: Recurring block defects, against what the guide warns about.
dimensions.five: Every failure this platform has met more than once is warned about here, in the terms a builder would recognise before they hit it — a write that returns an error and succeeds anyway, a filter accepted and ignored, a version that moves on restart.
dimensions.one: The guide restates the contract's requirements and warns about nothing. A team follows it exactly and still ships the defects we have already found in every other block, because the guide carries obligations and no experience.

dimensions.name: Honest about what the battery cannot settle
dimensions.evidence: What it says about R1, R7, R12, R13, R14.
dimensions.five: It says plainly that a clean conformance run is not a complete one, names the requirements a tool surface cannot establish, and tells a team to have them exercised in a real initiative.
dimensions.one: It presents `conformance` as the finish line, so a team reads a green result as done and ships with the behavioural requirements untested.

dimensions.name: Distinguishes what is theirs from what is ours
dimensions.evidence: Its guidance on usage skills and conduct.
dimensions.five: It tells a team what belongs in their skills — defects, ordering constraints, limits found by refusal — and what must not: conduct, which belongs to the flow running the work. It says when a skill should not exist at all because a live tool already returns better.
dimensions.one: It invites a team to ship their assistant's system prompt as a usage skill, which then imports another product's conduct rules into every flow that loads it.
